title: pool() can be DoS'd indefinitely if the donation phase's minUSDC requirement cannot be satisfied (USDC depeg, waUSDC redeem failure, or pool depletion), permanently locking sUSDS in the dispatcher
description:
pool() is an all-or-nothing transaction: the donation phase and the addLiquidity phase execute in a single unlockCallback. If the donation phase reverts (e.g., `require(usdcReceived >= minUSDC)` fails, or `IERC4626(waUsdc).redeem` reverts due to Aave pause / waUSDC frozen / Aave market liquidity exhaustion, or `IERC20(usdc).safeTransfer(batchMinter, ...)` reverts because batchMinter has been blocklisted on USDC), the entire unlockCallback reverts. There is no fallback path that skips the donation and proceeds to addLiquidity, no separate function to drain only sUSDS to the LP, and no way for the operator to lower minUSDC without re-signing.

The dispatcher's owner has `rescueERC20` as an escape hatch (line 314), which can transfer sUSDS out — but this is a centralisation lever (see also the centralization finding ECON-RAW-007). It is NOT an automated recovery: in an emergency the owner must manually unwind sUSDS via off-chain markets and re-route the value to LPs / batchMinter. During this period the protocol's primary value-flow mechanism is broken.

Additionally, the donation phase is gated on FOUR independent configuration variables being non-zero (`batchMinter`, `swapPool`, `waUsdc`, `usdc`) and `batchDonationSize > 0`. If any one of them is misconfigured or accidentally zeroed by the owner (setBatchMinter(address(0)) is explicitly allowed), donation is skipped — but if ALL are configured and donation is required to execute (e.g., the protocol's economic invariants assume donation always runs at a non-zero ratio), an unrelated revert in the donation path bricks pool() entirely.
exploit_path:
Scenario A — USDC blocklist of batchMinter:
USDC's Circle administrator blacklists an address. If batchMinter happens to be that address (or routes through it), `IERC20(usdc).safeTransfer(batchMinter, ...)` reverts. Until the owner calls setBatchMinter(...) to point to a new recipient (which requires an owner tx), every pool() call reverts.

Scenario B — Aave waUSDC market pause:
Aave can pause the waUSDC market (governance vote or emergency admin). `IERC4626(waUsdc).redeem(...)` reverts. pool() cannot progress until Aave unpauses. sUSDS continues to accumulate; if the Aave pause is long-lived, the protocol's batch-minting cadence is halted entirely.

Scenario C — donation pool depletion:
If the sUSDS/waUSDC Balancer pool's waUSDC side is drained by arbitrageurs or a JIT-LP-removal event, the donation swap may revert (out-of-range/insufficient-liquidity) or yield waUsdcReceived below minUSDC after unwrap. pool() reverts until pool conditions recover.

In each case, the SECONDARY damage is the LP-add phase is also blocked even though the sUSDS->phUSD pool is functional. The protocol could have at least completed the addLiquidity step but is blocked because the donation step is bundled.
mainnet_realism: USDC blacklist precedent: Circle has blacklisted addresses (e.g., Tornado Cash sanctions, Aug 2022, ~$75k frozen). Any address routed through the protocol's batchMinter — if it ever became sanctioned or accidentally received OFAC-tainted USDC — would brick pool(). Aave market pauses: Aave has historically paused markets (e.g., temporary freezes during the AAVE token vote in late 2022). Each of these is a low-probability but real-world event for which the protocol has no graceful degradation path.
recommendation: (1) Split donation and addLiquidity into separate functions (or add a bool skipDonation parameter) so an operator can complete the LP add even if the donation leg is impaired. (2) Wrap each external call (swap, sendTo, redeem, safeTransfer) in try/catch where the failure mode is a known temporary impairment; on failure, skip the donation slice and proceed to addLiquidity, leaving the donation-earmarked sUSDS as a separately-tracked deferred-donation ledger to be processed later. (3) Allow setBatchMinter(address(0)) to disable donations cleanly — current code already supports this — but document the operational playbook for emergency disablement, including a runbook for blocklist / pause events.
severity_rationale: Confirmed Medium. The donation + addLiquidity bundling means any revert in the donation leg (USDC blocklist of batchMinter, Aave waUSDC pause, donation pool depletion, USDC depeg pushing waUsdcReceived * shareRate below minUSDC) bricks the entire pool() execution. sUSDS continues to accumulate in the dispatcher with no path to forward to the LP. Even though the owner has rescueERC20 as an off-chain escape hatch, the protocol's primary value-flow mechanism (LP add) is halted by an unrelated impairment of the donation leg. Mainnet realism is strong: USDC has blacklist precedent, Aave has pause precedent, USDC has depeg precedent. This is clear 'function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted' — Medium per C4. Not High because assets are not directly at risk (they remain in the dispatcher; recovery requires owner action) and the impairment is triggered by external/exogenous events, not by an attacker action.
poc_notes: Production BalancerPoolerV2 used unmodified. Mocks scoped to non-Balancer surfaces that model real mainnet behaviour: BlocklistableUSDC (mirrors Circle FiatTokenV2.1's `blacklisted` mapping + 'Blacklistable: account is blacklisted' revert), PausableWaUSDC (mirrors Aave Pause Guardian — redeem() reverts when paused), MockBalancerVault (V3 cannot be ergonomically deployed in unit tests; bubbles inner reverts so the abort cascade matches mainnet). The bug demonstrated is control-flow: any revert inside the donation leg bricks the entire unlockCallback. 5 tests pass: (1) healthy sanity baseline; (2) USDC blocklist DoS — pool() reverts with 'Blacklistable: account is blacklisted'; (3) Aave waUSDC pause DoS — reverts with 'PAUSED: aave market frozen', then auto-recovers when unpaused; (4) donation pool depleted — reverts with 'BAL: swap pool depleted'; (5) recovery requires owner intervention (setBatchMinter(0)). No imagined AMM behaviour — only revert propagation.
